test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 30 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct option to specify the meaning of the highlighted idiom.

"I know you are ready. **Go break a leg now**."

options.text: Ask someone not to go for a task

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Say Good Luck to someone**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Break a leg"** is commonly used to wish someone good luck before they perform or attempt something. (शुभकामनाएं देना) • **Example:** Before her big performance, her friends said, "Break a leg!" to encourage her. • The highlighted idiom does not literally mean to break a leg but is instead a way of expressing encouragement and well-wishing. (हिंदी में: शुभकामनाएं देने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता है) • **Example:** "Break a leg! You'll do great in your interview." Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Say Good Luck to someone**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: Ask someone not to go for a task** (किसी को काम करने से मना करना) • **Example:** This option is incorrect as "Break a leg" does not mean to discourage or stop someone. • **Option 3: Say Bad Luck to someone** (किसी को दुर्भाग्य की कामना करना) • **Example:** This option is incorrect because the idiom "Break a leg" conveys good luck, not bad luck. • **Option 4: Not saying anything to someone** (किसी से कुछ भी न कहना) • **Example:** This option is incorrect because "Break a leg" is a phrase actively used to wish someone good luck. 34:Te81, The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Take risks.
